title: Mary Prince
summary: Born into slavery in Bermuda around 1788, Mary Prince was held in Bermuda, Grand Turk Island and Antigua before her enslavers brought her to London in 1828. She left their household, found refuge at the Moravian mission in Hatton Garden, and later worked for Thomas Pringle of the Anti-Slavery Society. Her 1831 History of Mary Prince was the first narrative by a Black woman published in Britain.

uncertainty.note: Birth is given as 1788 by the London Museum and as c. 1788 by Encyclopedia.com. Encyclopedia.com gives her death as after 1833; the London Museum gives no end date, so 1833 is the last year the opened sources record her.

as_recorded.value: In 1828, Prince was brought from Antigua to London

where.modern_name: Hatton Garden, Holborn, London, England (pinned to the Moravian mission where she found refuge in London, the setting of her documented anti-slavery work; she was born at Brackish Pond, Bermuda)
where.historical_name: Hatton Garden, London, in the British Empire, where a Moravian mission stood in 1828

importance.justification: The London Museum calls her book the first narrative of a Black woman published in Britain; her story was brought to the Anti-Slavery Society.

audience_note: This record describes a life in slavery, including sale, cruelty and violence; it is drawn from her own dictated account.

reviewer_note: Sources disagree on how she gained freedom: the London Museum says she walked out of the household and was technically free in England; Encyclopedia.com says she purchased her freedom. The pin is a street in London, not the mission building; her years in Bermuda and Antigua are not pinned.
